Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates significant cardiomegaly and prominent central pulmonary arteries, which are characteristic radiographic signs of long-standing pulmonary artery hypertension. This chronic elevation in pulmonary pressure leads to right ventricular hypertrophy/dilation (causing the cardiomegaly) and weakens the vessel wall, predisposing the patient to complications like a pulmonary artery pseudoaneurysm.
